dimensions.name: Slicing the surface into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking a huge, interdependent feature set into an ordered hierarchy of sub-systems, each with a concrete done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of loosely coupled subsystems (persistence, engine core, spill, xlsx, collab, SPA), an unstructured attack strands half-finished features and blocks the foundational pieces (recompute graph) that everything else depends on.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat to-do list of feature names with no dependency ordering and no per-item definition of done.
anchors.5: Identifies major subsystems and sequences them sensibly (health/persistence → cell CRUD → dependency recompute → functions → advanced surfaces), each with a rough acceptance check.
anchors.8: A dependency-aware milestone plan where foundational layers (dirty-only topological recompute, wire contract) are stabilized before dependents, each milestone with an explicit pass condition tied to the harness or a self-written check.
anchors.10: A layered plan that also reasons about cross-cutting risk (spill ↔ recompute ↔ xlsx ↔ collab must share one cell model), sizes milestones to keep a working server at every step, and re-plans milestone boundaries as coupling is discovered.

dimensions.name: Building checks beyond the smoke suite

dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec warns the dev_tests are a non-exhaustive smoke suite and grading uses a held-out LibreOffice corpus; passing run.sh proves almost nothing, so the agent must manufacture its own correctness signal for functions, spill, errors, and xlsx round-trips.

anchors.0: Never runs anything, or assumes code is correct because it was written.

anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite plus ad hoc manual checks of a few endpoints and formulas it just wrote.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks for high-risk areas the smoke suite can't cover — error-sentinel propagation, spill/#SPILL!, iterative convergence, openpyxl re-import, performance bars — and validates function outputs against known-correct values.
anchors.10: Stands up a reusable verification loop (oracle-style comparisons for formula values, round-trip export→import assertions, load/latency probes for the perf clauses) and uses it continuously to catch regressions across subsystems, not just at the end.

dimensions.name: Tracking coverage across a huge horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across scores of features and detecting stalls/circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog is enormous and easy to lose track of; without a running ledger the agent silently drops whole function families or endpoints and burns the horizon re-debugging one corner.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs left; features silently forgotten, no awareness when stuck.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; rediscovers unfinished work by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as pieces land.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate live ledger of implemented-vs-remaining across the catalog and endpoints, and notices when it's looping on one bug rather than progressing.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles remaining work against remaining effort, explicitly triages when time-boxed, and recognizes thrash early enough to switch tactics or defer a subsystem rather than sinking the horizon into one stubborn corner.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design, library choice, or approach when probes/tests reveal reality differs from expectation, rather than pushing ahead on a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Big bets here (formula-eval library, spill data model, xlsx library, recompute algorithm) can be falsified mid-build; a rigid agent that discovers its cell model can't represent spill ghosts or its lib can't emit openpyxl-readable styles must restructure, not paper over.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps building on a disproven assumption until it collapses.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local patches that don't address the wrong underlying model.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the real cause, and will change a local approach when clearly wrong.
anchors.8: Treats surprising results as signal: revisits the contract or design, and makes deliberate structural changes (e.g. reworking the cell model or swapping a library) when a foundational assumption is falsified.
anchors.10: Anticipates fragile bets, validates them early with cheap probes, and when one breaks re-plans downstream milestones coherently — updating the mental model, the plan, and the verification checks together rather than barrelling ahead.

dimensions.name: Breadth allocation against a hidden grader
dimensions.description: Strategically allocating effort across a vast feature catalog to maximize expected graded coverage under uncertainty about which corners the hidden suite weights.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Being graded on a much larger hidden suite than is visible makes it a resource-allocation problem: over-polishing one exotic function family while leaving common lookups, error propagation, or persistence half-built wastes the horizon on low-expected-value work.

anchors.0: Effort distribution is arbitrary; sinks disproportionate time into a narrow corner while core surfaces stay unbuilt.
anchors.3: Implements whatever is top-of-mind with no reasoning about coverage value or grading likelihood.
anchors.5: Prioritizes obviously high-value, broadly-tested areas (core engine, common functions, persistence, wire contract) before exotic ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about expected graded value — covering the breadth of function families and endpoints at working quality before deep-polishing any single one, and consciously defers low-probability corners.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate breadth-first-then-deepen strategy calibrated to the hidden-suite risk: ensures every major surface returns plausibly-correct results, then reinvests remaining budget where correctness risk and likely test weight are highest, adjusting as evidence accrues.

task_read: A very large, long-horizon build: a full Excel-clone server (HTTP+JSON API, SPA, WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, dynamic-array spill semantics, error sentinels, iterative calc, goal seek, xlsx/CSV round-trip, pivots, conditional formatting, locale input, data validation, plus hard performance budgets and restart persistence. The exact wire contract is undocumented and must be reverse-engineered from an existing first-party client (`/dev_tests/helpers.py`), and grading is against a large hidden suite plus a LibreOffice ground-truth corpus. Difficulty comes from breadth (many loosely-coupled subsystems), an inferred contract, and correctness against external oracles — so a skilled practitioner would invest heavily in orientation, milestone decomposition, and self-built verification, and sustain progress-tracking and course-correction across dozens of hours.

anchors.10: Builds a precise, verified model of the whole contract from the client, proactively probes edge cases (locale separators, ghost-write rejection, iterative fixed points) against authoritative behavior, and returns to re-read sources whenever a hidden-suite mismatch reveals a gap — orientation is continuous, not one-shot.

dimensions.name: Subsystem sequencing & done-criteria

anchors.10: A layered milestone hierarchy that sequences ~150 functions and features by risk and dependency, defines a verifiable acceptance check per milestone, and is revised as reality shifts — enabling steady, measurable advance across the full horizon without losing coverage.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness checks beyond the smoke suite

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge surface

dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and a dozen subsystems over a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-cover, or leave whole families unimplemented; accurate done-vs-remaining tracking is what sustains progress.

anchors.5: Keeps a running checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as items complete.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, frequently-updated status of every function family and feature (done/partial/failing), and notices when it is stuck re-debugging the same area.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise coverage ledger across the whole horizon, distinguishes verified-passing from merely-written, catches circular/thrashing debugging early, and uses the ledger to re-prioritize remaining work under time pressure.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on contract/semantic mismatches
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when tests, oracle comparisons, or perf measurements reveal a wrong assumption — rather than pushing ahead on a falsified contract or algorithm.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Because the contract is inferred and correctness is judged externally, mismatches are expected; the ability to localize the wrong assumption and fix the design (e.g. recompute ordering, spill model, wire shape) determines whether the agent converges or accumulates broken subsystems.

anchors.0: Ignores failing checks or repeats the same fix; barrels ahead on falsified assumptions.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with local patches but doesn't revisit the underlying wrong model.
anchors.5: When a test or comparison fails, diagnoses and fixes the specific issue, adjusting nearby design as needed.
anchors.8: Traces failures to root causes, revises the affected design (contract shape, dependency/topo algorithm, spill/perf approach) deliberately, and re-verifies the fix without regressing other areas.
anchors.10: Treats divergences as signal: re-examines the inferred contract or algorithmic model when evidence contradicts it, makes principled structural changes early rather than accreting hacks, and confirms the correction propagates cleanly across dependent subsystems.

dimensions.name: Keeping the live server runnable end-to-end
dimensions.description: Ensuring start.sh actually boots, health returns ok, and the app stays integrated and runnable throughout, rather than accumulating code that has never been executed together.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is entirely against a live server (`bash /app/start.sh`, `/api/health`, REST/WS/SPA); a huge codebase that was never actually booted end-to-end scores zero regardless of internal quality, so continuous integration/boot discipline is a distinct process demand here.

anchors.0: Never runs start.sh end-to-end; discovers boot/wiring failures (if ever) only at the end.
anchors.3: Boots the server rarely; large amounts of code integrated in one late big-bang.
anchors.5: Gets a runnable server early and re-launches it periodically to confirm health and basic endpoints still work.
anchors.8: Maintains a continuously bootable server, verifies health and key surfaces (REST, WS, SPA, persistence-after-restart) as subsystems land, and catches integration breakage promptly.
anchors.10: Treats end-to-end runnability as an invariant: a thin vertical slice boots very early, every milestone is validated against the live process including restart persistence, and integration regressions are caught the moment they appear.
